teaser: A researcher, a curator and a journalist on a schedule, the QR handshake that gives each agent its key, and why it has to be built slowly.
core_idea: The PHP story site is updated by three scheduled agents in a chain, from raw captures to curated evidence to the published site; because neither Claude's scheduled tasks nor ChatGPT gives an agent an identity or a secret, each agent session gets its vault key once by a QR handshake on pki.sgit.ai and is then woken on a schedule, a workflow that is almost working and is being built slowly, in its genesis stage.

quotes.text: It is a slightly mad solution, and a lovely one.
Collection is easy. Collection with an identity, a secret and a schedule is not.
Nothing an agent does on a schedule is outside a task someone queued.
quotes.why: The schedule vault: control is the queue.

figures.caption: Three agents, three stores, one site: the researcher writes the source watch (oq9gflln, raw captures); the curator promotes what holds into the evidence vault (3ytzxm3g, 227 curated sources); the journalist updates the site from it. The schedule vault (weic8imn, public) records who runs, when, and what each run did.

One handshake, then a schedule: the agent makes a session key and pins the root; shows its fingerprint and QR; the editor checks it and seals the vault key to it on pki.sgit.ai; the agent opens it, clones the vault and deletes the file; a scheduled task wakes the same session.

Almost working, on the evening of 23 October: what works (the researcher's 40 recorded runs, the handshake, the schedule vault, the journalist's views, the last-checked stamp), what is set up but not yet proven (the curator's wakes, run records written by the agents themselves, the researcher's schedule), and what is missing.
